title.zh: 卷三十九 雜傳第二十七: 王鎔 羅紹威 王處直 劉守光
title.en: Volume 39 Miscellaneous Biographies 19: Wang Rong, Luo Shaowei, Wang Chuzhi, Liu Shouguang
title.raw: 卷三十九 雜傳第二十七: 王鎔 羅紹威 王處直 劉守光 Volume 39 Miscellaneous Biographies 19: Wang Rong, Luo Shaowei, Wang Chuzhi, Liu Shouguang

sentences.zh: 王镕，其先回鶻阿布思之遺種，曰沒諾幹，為鎮州王武俊騎將，武俊錄以為子，遂冒姓王氏。

translations.literal: Wang Rong: his ancestors were descendants of the Uyghur Abu Si, named Mo Nuogan, a cavalry officer of Wang Wujun of Zhenzhou; Wujun adopted him as a son, and he took the surname Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong traced his line to Mo Nuogan, a survivor of the Uyghur chief Abu Si. Mo Nuogan served Wang Wujun of Zhenzhou as a mounted officer; Wujun adopted him, and the family took the name Wang.

sentences.zh: 沒諾幹子曰末垣活，末垣活子曰升，升子曰廷湊，廷湊子曰元達，元達子曰紹鼎、紹懿，紹鼎子曰景崇。

translations.literal: Mo Nuogan’s son was Mo Yuanhuo; Mo Yuanhuo’s son was Sheng; Sheng’s son was Tingcou; Tingcou’s son was Yuanda; Yuanda’s sons were Shaoding and Shaoyi; Shaoding’s son was Jingchong.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Nuogan begat Mo Yuanhuo, who begat Sheng, then Tingcou, then Yuanda. Yuanda had Shaoding and Shaoyi; Shaoding begat Jingchong.

sentences.zh: 自升以上三世，常為鎮州騎將，自景崇以上四世五人，皆為成德軍節度使。

translations.literal: From Sheng upward for three generations they were constantly Zhenzhou cavalry officers; from Jingchong upward for four generations five men all were military commissioners of the Chengde army.
translations.idiomatic: For three generations before Sheng the family held cavalry commands at Zhenzhou; for four generations from Jingchong, five men in succession ruled Chengde.

sentences.zh: 景崇官至守太尉，封常山郡王，唐中和二年卒。

translations.literal: Jingchong reached the office of Acting Grand Marshal, was enfeoffed Prince of Changshan, and died in the second year of Tang Zhonghe.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong rose to Acting Grand Marshal and Prince of Changshan; he died in Zhonghe 2 of Tang.

sentences.zh: 子镕立，年十歲。

translations.literal: His son Rong succeeded, ten years old.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rong succeeded him at the age of ten.

sentences.zh: 是時，晉新有太原，李匡威據幽州，王處存據中山，赫連鐸據大同，孟方立據邢臺，四面豪傑並起而交爭。

translations.literal: At that time Jin had newly taken Taiyuan; Li Kuangwei held Youzhou, Wang Chucun held Zhongshan, Helian Duo held Datong, and Meng Fangli held Xingtai—heroes rose on every side and fought one another.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had just secured Taiyuan. Li Kuangwei held Youzhou, Wang Chucun Zhongshan, Helian Duo Datong, Meng Fangli Xingtai—warlords sprang up on all sides and tore at one another.

sentences.zh: 镕介於其間，而承祖父百年之業，士馬強而畜積富，為唐累世藩臣。

translations.literal: Rong stood between them, yet inherited his grandfather’s enterprise of a hundred years: strong soldiers and horses, rich stores—a Tang frontier house for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Rong sat in the middle of them all, heir to a century of Wang power: strong cavalry, deep granaries, a Tang vassal line for generations.

sentences.zh: 故镕年雖少，藉其世家以取重，四方諸鎮廢立承繼，有請於唐者，皆因镕以聞。

translations.literal: Thus though Rong was young, he drew weight from his house; when the circuits sought Tang’s approval for deposition, succession, or appointment, the petition always went through Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Young as he was, the Wang name gave him weight. Whenever a circuit asked the court to confirm a change of ruler, the word passed through Rong.

sentences.zh: 初，匡威悅其弟匡儔之婦美而淫之，匡儔怒，及其救镕也，誘其軍亂而自立。

translations.literal: Earlier Kuangwei had coveted his brother Kuangchou’s wife for her beauty and lain with her; Kuangchou was enraged. When he came to rescue Rong he incited the army to mutiny and set himself up as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuangwei had taken his brother Kuangchou’s wife and seduced her; Kuangchou burned with anger. When he marched to save Rong he turned the troops against his brother and seized Youzhou for himself.

sentences.zh: 匡威內慚不敢還，乃以符印歸其弟，而將奔於京師。

translations.literal: Ashamed within, Kuangwei dared not return; he returned the seals to his brother and prepared to flee to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Too ashamed to face his men, Kuangwei handed the seals to Kuangchou and set out for the capital.

sentences.zh: 行至深州，镕德匡威救己，使人邀之，館於梅子園，以父事之。

translations.literal: When he reached Shenzhou, Rong, grateful that Kuangwei had saved him, sent men to invite him and lodged him at Meizi Garden, treating him as a father.
translations.idiomatic: At Shenzhou, Rong—mindful that Kuangwei had saved him—sent for him and housed him at Meizi Garden, honoring him like a parent.

sentences.zh: 匡威客李正抱者，少遊燕、趙間，每徘徊常山，愛之不能去。

translations.literal: Among Kuangwei’s followers was Li Zhengbao, who in youth had roamed Yan and Zhao and, lingering at Changshan, loved the place and could not leave.
translations.idiomatic: One of Kuangwei’s companions was Li Zhengbao. As a young man he had wandered Yan and Zhao; each time he passed Changshan he lingered, unable to tear himself away.

sentences.zh: 正抱、匡威皆失國無聊，相與登城西高閣，顧覽山川，泫然而泣，乃與匡威謀劫而代之。

translations.literal: Zhengbao and Kuangwei, both exiles with nothing to do, climbed the high pavilion west of the city, looked over the hills and rivers, wept, and plotted to seize Rong’s place.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengbao and Kuangwei, both landless and idle, climbed the western tower, gazed over the landscape until they wept, and hatched a plan to seize Rong by force.

sentences.zh: 因詐為忌日，镕去衛從，晨詣館慰，坐定，甲士自幕後出，持镕兩袖，镕曰：「吾國賴公而存，誠無以報厚德，今日之事，是所甘心。

translations.literal: They feigned a day of mourning; Rong left his guards and came at dawn to the lodge to offer condolences. Once seated, armored men burst from behind the curtain and seized both his sleeves. Rong said: “Our state survived only through you—I have no way to repay such kindness. What you do today I accept willingly.
translations.idiomatic: They staged a memorial day. Rong came at dawn without escort to comfort Kuangwei at the lodge. As he sat down, soldiers in armor rushed from behind the screen and gripped his sleeves. Rong said: “You preserved our house—I could never repay you. Do as you will; I submit.

sentences.zh: 」因叩頭以位與匡威。

translations.literal: ” He then kowtowed and yielded the throne to Kuangwei.
translations.idiomatic: ” He kowtowed and offered Kuangwei the command.

sentences.zh: 匡威素少镕，以謂無能為也，因與镕方轡詣府，將代其位。

translations.literal: Kuangwei had always looked down on the young Rong and thought him incapable; he rode side by side with Rong to the headquarters, about to take his place.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangwei had always despised the boy and thought him harmless. He rode beside Rong to the yamen, ready to replace him.

sentences.zh: 行過親事營，軍士閉門大噪，天雨震電，暴風拔木，屋瓦皆飛。

translations.literal: As they passed the personal-guard camp the soldiers shut the gates and raised a great clamor; rain fell, thunder rolled, a gale uprooted trees, and roof tiles flew through the air.
translations.idiomatic: Passing the household guard camp, the troops slammed the gates and roared. Rain poured, lightning split the sky, wind tore up trees, and tiles flew from the roofs.

sentences.zh: 屠者墨君和望見镕，識之，從缺垣中躍出，挾镕於馬，負之而走，亂軍擊殺匡威、正抱，燕人皆死。

translations.literal: The butcher Mo Junhe saw Rong, recognized him, leaped through a gap in the wall, seized him onto a horse, and carried him away; the mutineers killed Kuangwei and Zhengbao, and all the Yan men with them died.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Junhe the butcher spotted Rong, knew him, scrambled through a broken wall, hauled him onto a horse, and fled. The rebels killed Kuangwei and Zhengbao; every man from Yan died with them.

sentences.zh: 匡儔雖憾其兄，而陽以大義責镕甚急。

translations.literal: Though Kuangchou resented his brother, outwardly he pressed Rong hard with righteous blame.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangchou hated his brother, yet in public he rebuked Rong in the name of justice.

sentences.zh: 镕既失燕援，而晉軍急攻平山，劫镕以盟，镕遂與晉和。

translations.literal: Rong, having lost Yan’s support, faced Jin’s urgent assault on Pingshan; Jin took him hostage to force an alliance, and Rong made peace with Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off from Yan, Rong faced a fierce Jin attack on Pingshan. Jin held him to ransom for peace, and he submitted.

sentences.zh: 其後梁太祖下晉邢、洺、磁三州，乃為書詔镕，使絕晉而歸梁，镕依違不決。

translations.literal: Later Liang Taizu took Jin’s Xing, Ming, and Ci prefectures and sent an edict ordering Rong to break with Jin and return to Liang; Rong wavered, unable to decide.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Taizu seized Xing, Ming, and Ci from Jin he wrote Rong demanding he abandon Jin for Liang. Rong hesitated.

sentences.zh: 晉將李嗣昭復取洺州，梁太祖擊敗嗣昭，嗣昭棄洺州走。

translations.literal: Jin’s general Li Sizhao retook Mingzhou; Liang Taizu defeated Sizhao, and Sizhao abandoned Mingzhou and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao of Jin retook Mingzhou. Liang Taizu routed him, and Sizhao abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 梁獲其輜重，得镕與嗣昭書，多道梁事，太祖怒，因移兵常山，顧謂葛從周曰：「得鎮州以與爾，爾為我先鋒。

translations.literal: Liang captured the baggage train and found letters between Rong and Sizhao that spoke often of Liang’s affairs; the Taizu was furious, shifted his army to Changshan, and said to Ge Congzhou: “I give you Zhenzhou—be my vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Liang took the supply train and found Rong’s letters to Sizhao, full of talk about Liang. Taizu flew into a rage, marched on Changshan, and told Ge Congzhou: “Zhenzhou is yours—lead the van.

sentences.zh: 」從周至臨城，中流矢，臥輿中，梁軍大沮。

translations.literal: ” Congzhou reached Lincheng, took an arrow in the stream, and lay in a litter; the Liang army was greatly discouraged.
translations.idiomatic: ” At Lincheng Congzhou took an arrow and had to be carried in a litter; Liang’s army lost heart.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖自將傅城下，焚其南關，镕懼，顧其屬曰：「事急矣！

translations.literal: Liang Taizu personally led the assault below the walls and burned the south gate. Rong was afraid and said to his men: “Matters are desperate!
translations.idiomatic: Taizu himself pressed the siege and fired the south gate. Rong, terrified, turned to his officers: “This is the end!

sentences.zh: 奈何？

translations.literal: What can we do?
translations.idiomatic: What can we do?

sentences.zh: 」判官周式，辨士也，對曰：「此難與力爭，而可以理奪也。

translations.literal: ” His staff officer Zhou Shi, a man of eloquence, replied: “This is not a fight to win by force—but it can be won by reason.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shi, a gifted speaker, answered: “You cannot beat them in battle. You may yet move them with argument.

sentences.zh: 」式與梁太祖有舊，因請入梁軍。

translations.literal: Shi had old ties with Liang Taizu and asked to enter the Liang camp.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was an old acquaintance of Taizu’s and asked leave to go to the Liang lines.

sentences.zh: 太祖望見式，罵曰：「吾常以書招镕不來，今吾至此，而爾為說客，晚矣！

translations.literal: Taizu saw him from afar and cursed: “I wrote again and again summoning Rong—he would not come. Now that I am here you play the envoy? Too late!
translations.idiomatic: Taizu spotted him and raged: “I wrote Rong again and again—he ignored me. Now I am at his gates and you come as a go-between? It is too late!

sentences.zh: 且晉吾仇也，而镕附之，吾知李嗣昭在城中，可使先出。

translations.literal: And Jin is my enemy, yet Rong clings to them. I know Li Sizhao is in the city—have him come out first.
translations.idiomatic: Jin is my enemy, and Rong sides with them. I know Sizhao is inside—send him out first.

sentences.zh: 」乃以所得镕與嗣昭書示式，式進曰：「梁欲取一鎮州而止乎，而欲成霸業於天下也？

translations.literal: He then showed Shi the captured letters. Shi advanced and said: “Does Liang mean to take only one Zhenzhou—or to win empire under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: He flung the letters before Shi. Shi stepped forward: “Does Liang want one prefecture—or the realm?

sentences.zh: 且霸者責人以義而不私，今天子在上，諸侯守封睦鄰，所以息爭，且休民也。

translations.literal: A hegemon holds men to righteousness, not to private gain. Today the Son of Heaven sits above; the feudatories guard their fiefs and keep peace with their neighbors—that is how strife ends and the people rest.
translations.idiomatic: A true conqueror judges by duty, not spite. The Son of Heaven still reigns; the circuits hold their borders and live as neighbors—that is how wars end and the people breathe.

sentences.zh: 昔曹公破袁紹，得魏將吏與紹書，悉焚之，此英雄之事乎！

translations.literal: When Duke Cao broke Yuan Shao he found letters between Shao and his own officers and burned them all—is that not the act of a hero?
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao crushed Yuan Shao he found his officers’ letters to the enemy and burned them—is that not how a great man acts?

sentences.zh: 今梁知兵舉無名，而假嗣昭以為辭。

translations.literal: Now Liang knows this campaign has no good name and uses Sizhao only as a pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Liang knows this war has no just cause and hides behind Sizhao’s name.

sentences.zh: 且王氏五世六公撫有此士，豈無死士，而待嗣昭乎？

translations.literal: The Wang house for five generations and six lords has held this land—do you think they have no men who would die for them, waiting on Sizhao?
translations.idiomatic: Five generations of Wangs have ruled this soil—do you imagine they have no loyal dead, and that only Sizhao stands between you and them?

sentences.zh: 」太祖大喜，起牽式衣而撫之曰：「吾言戲耳。

translations.literal: ” The Taizu was greatly pleased, rose, took Shi by the robe, and stroked him, saying: “My words were in jest.
translations.idiomatic: ” Taizu laughed with delight, rose, took Shi by the sleeve, and said: “I was only testing you.

sentences.zh: 」因延式於上坐，議與镕和。

translations.literal: He seated Shi in the place of honor and discussed peace with Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Shi the seat of honor and opened talks for peace with Rong.

sentences.zh: 镕以子昭祚為質，梁太祖以女妻之。

translations.literal: Rong sent his son Zhaozuo as hostage; Liang Taizu gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Rong sent his son Zhaozuo as hostage; Taizu married him to a Liang princess.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，封镕趙王。

translations.literal: When the Taizu took the throne he enfeoffed Rong Prince of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu became emperor he made Rong Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 镕祖母喪，諸鎮皆吊，梁使者見晉使在館，還言趙王有二誌。

translations.literal: When Rong’s grandmother died every circuit sent condolences; a Liang envoy saw a Jin envoy in the lodge and reported that the Prince of Zhao had two minds.
translations.idiomatic: At his grandmother’s funeral every circuit sent mourners. A Liang envoy saw Jin’s envoy at the same guesthouse and reported that the Zhao prince was playing both sides.

sentences.zh: 是時，魏博羅紹威卒，梁因欲盡取河北，開平四年冬，遣供奉官杜廷隱監魏博將夏諲，以兵三千襲深、冀二州，以王景仁為北面行營招討使。

translations.literal: At that time Luo Shaowei of Wei Bo had died; Liang wished to take all of Hebei. In the winter of Kaiping 4 he sent the palace attendant Du Tingyin to supervise the Wei Bo general Xia Yin with three thousand men in a surprise attack on Shen and Ji, and made Wang Jingren commander of the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shaowei of Wei Bo had just died, and Liang aimed to swallow Hebei. In the winter of Kaiping 4 Taizu sent Du Tingyin with Xia Yin and three thousand Wei Bo troops to strike Shen and Ji, and appointed Wang Jingren to command the northern front.

sentences.zh: 镕懼，乞兵於晉。

translations.literal: Rong was afraid and begged troops from Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Rong begged Jin for aid.

sentences.zh: 晉人擊敗景仁於柏鄉，梁遂失鎮、定，而莊宗由此益強，北破幽、燕，南並魏博，镕常以兵從。

translations.literal: Jin defeated Jingren at Bocheng; Liang then lost Zhen and Ding, and Zhuangzong grew stronger—north he broke You and Yan, south he absorbed Wei Bo, and Rong often marched with him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin routed Jingren at Bocheng. Liang lost Zhen and Ding; Zhuangzong grew mighty—conquering You and Yan in the north, swallowing Wei Bo in the south—with Rong’s armies often at his side.

sentences.zh: 镕德晉甚。

translations.literal: Rong was deeply grateful to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Rong owed Jin a deep debt of gratitude.

sentences.zh: 明年，會莊宗於承天軍，奉觴為壽，莊宗以镕父友，尊禮之，酒酣為镕歌，拔佩刀斷衣而盟，許以女妻镕子昭誨。

translations.literal: The next year he met Zhuangzong at Chengtian Army, raised a cup for his long life; Zhuangzong, treating him as his father’s friend, honored him. When the wine was deep he sang for Rong, drew his saber, cut his robe, and swore brotherhood, promising his daughter to Rong’s son Zhaohui.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he met Zhuangzong at Chengtian Army and toasted his health. Zhuangzong, who had known Rong’s father, treated him with ceremony. Drunk, he sang for Rong, drew his blade, cut his own robe for a blood oath, and pledged his daughter to Rong’s son Zhaohui.

sentences.zh: 镕為人仁而不武，未嘗敢為兵先，佗兵攻趙，常藉鄰兵為救。

translations.literal: Rong was benevolent and unwarlike; he never dared lead the van. When other armies attacked Zhao he always borrowed neighbors for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was gentle and no soldier; he never led from the front. Whenever Zhao was attacked he called on neighboring armies to save him.

sentences.zh: 當是時，諸鎮相弊於戰爭，而趙獨安，樂王氏之無事，都人士女褒衣博帶，務誇侈為嬉遊。

translations.literal: While the circuits wore one another down in war, Zhao alone remained at peace; the capital’s gentry and women wore loose robes and broad sashes and made a sport of display.
translations.idiomatic: While the other circuits bled one another dry, Zhao alone stayed quiet. In the capital, men and women dressed in flowing silks and turned luxury into pastime.

sentences.zh: 镕尤驕於富貴，又好左道，煉丹藥，求長生，與道士王若訥留遊西山，登王母祠，使婦人維錦繡牽持而上。

translations.literal: Rong was proudest of his wealth; he also loved heterodox ways, refined elixirs, and sought long life. With the Daoist Wang Ruone he lingered on West Mountain, climbed the Queen Mother shrine, and had women in brocade hold the ropes to pull him up.
translations.idiomatic: Rong flaunted his riches and dabbled in occult arts, brewing elixirs in search of immortality. With the Daoist Wang Ruone he toured West Mountain, climbed the Queen Mother temple, and had women in embroidered silks haul him up by rope.

sentences.zh: 每出，逾月忘歸，任其政於宦者。

translations.literal: Each time he went out he forgot to return for more than a month and left government to the eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: He would be gone for months at a time and leave the realm to his eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 宦者石希蒙與镕同臥起。

translations.literal: The eunuch Shi Ximeng shared his bed and his waking hours.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Shi Ximeng slept and rose at his side.

sentences.zh: 天祐十八年冬，镕自西山宿鶻營莊，將還府，希蒙止之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eighteenth year of Tianyou, Rong lodged at Gull Camp Manor on his way back from West Mountain; as he was about to return to headquarters, Ximeng stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Tianyou 18 Rong stayed at Gull Camp Manor on the road back from West Mountain. When he tried to return to the yamen, Ximeng barred him.

sentences.zh: 宦者李弘規諫曰：「今晉王身自暴露以親矢石，而大王竭軍國之用為遊畋之資，開城空宮，逾月不返，使一失閉門不納從者，大王欲何歸乎？

translations.literal: The eunuch Li Honggui remonstrated: “Now the Prince of Jin exposes his own body to arrows and stones, while you drain the state for hunting. You leave the city gates open and the palace empty, gone for more than a month. If once they shut the gates and refuse your followers, where will you go?
translations.idiomatic: Li Honggui warned him: “The Prince of Jin fights in person under fire, while you spend the treasury on pleasure. You leave the walls unmanned and the palace empty for months. If they lock the gates and turn you away, where will you sleep?

sentences.zh: 」镕懼，促駕，希蒙固止之。

translations.literal: Rong was afraid and urged his carriage on; Ximeng firmly held him back.
translations.idiomatic: Rong grew afraid and ordered his carriage; Ximeng would not let him go.

sentences.zh: 弘規怒，遣親事軍將蘇漢衡率兵擐甲露刃於帳前曰：「軍士勞矣！

translations.literal: Honggui in anger sent the personal-guard general Su Hanheng with troops in armor and bare blades before the tent, saying: “The soldiers are weary!
translations.idiomatic: Honggui in fury sent Su Hanheng of the household guard with armored men and naked swords to the tent: “The troops are exhausted!

sentences.zh: 願從王歸。

translations.literal: We wish to follow the prince home.
translations.idiomatic: They want to escort you home.”

sentences.zh: 」弘規繼而進曰：「惑王者希蒙也，請殺之以謝軍士！

translations.literal: Honggui then advanced and said: “The one who has misled the prince is Ximeng—kill him to answer the soldiers!
translations.idiomatic: Honggui pressed on: “Ximeng is the one who led you astray—kill him and appease the men!”

sentences.zh: 」镕不答，弘規呼镕甲士斬希蒙首，擲於镕前，镕懼，遽歸。

translations.literal: Rong did not answer; Honggui called Rong’s guards to cut off Ximeng’s head and throw it before him. Rong was afraid and hurried home.
translations.idiomatic: Rong said nothing. Honggui ordered the guards to behead Ximeng and fling the head at Rong’s feet. Rong fled home in terror.

sentences.zh: 使其子昭祚與大將張文禮族弘規、漢衡，收其偏將下獄，窮究反狀，親軍皆懼。

translations.literal: He had his son Zhaozuo and the great general Zhang Wenli execute the families of Honggui and Hanheng, imprisoned their subordinate generals, and investigated the rebellion to the end; the personal guard were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his son Zhaozuo and Zhang Wenli to wipe out Honggui’s and Hanheng’s kin, jailed their officers, and hunted the plot to its roots. The household guard trembled.

sentences.zh: 文禮誘以為亂，夜半，親軍千餘人逾垣而入，镕方與道士焚香受箓，軍士斬镕首，袖之而出，因縱火焚其宮室，遂滅王氏之族。

translations.literal: Wenli incited them to mutiny. At midnight more than a thousand guards scaled the wall and entered; Rong was just burning incense with a Daoist to receive a talisman when the soldiers cut off his head, tucked it in a sleeve, and left, then set fire and burned the palace—thus the Wang clan was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Wenli turned their fear into revolt. After midnight a thousand guards poured over the wall. Rong was receiving a Daoist talisman when they struck off his head, hid it in a sleeve, and torched the palace. The Wang line ended that night.

sentences.zh: 镕小子昭誨，年十歲，其軍士有德镕者，藏之穴中，亂定，髡其發，被以僧衣，遇湖南人李震，匿昭誨於茶籠中，載之湖南，依南嶽為浮圖，易名崇隱。

translations.literal: Rong’s young son Zhaohui was ten. Soldiers who had owed Rong kindness hid him in a cave; when the turmoil ended they shaved his head and dressed him as a monk. He met a Hunan man named Li Zhen, who hid Zhaohui in a tea basket and carried him to Hunan; he became a monk on South Mountain under the name Chongyin.
translations.idiomatic: Rong’s son Zhaohui was ten. Men who remembered Rong’s kindness hid him in a pit; when order returned they tonsured him and clothed him as a novice. A Hunanese named Li Zhen hid him in a tea crate and took him south. On South Mountain he entered the clergy as Chongyin.

sentences.zh: 明宗時，昭誨已長，思歸，而镕故將符習為宣武軍節度使，震以歸習，習表於朝。

translations.literal: In Mingzong’s time Zhaohui had grown and wished to return. Rong’s old general Fu Xi was military commissioner of Xuanwu; Zhen brought him to Xi, and Xi memorialized the court.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong, Zhaohui was grown and longed for home. Fu Xi, once Rong’s officer, now commanded Xuanwu. Li Zhen delivered the boy to him, and Fu Xi reported to court.

sentences.zh: 昭誨自稱前成德軍中軍使以見，拜考功郎中、司農少卿。

translations.literal: Zhaohui presented himself as former central-army commander of Chengde, was made Reviewing Affairs Cadre and Vice Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaohui appeared as Chengde’s former central-army commander and received office as Reviewing Affairs cadre and Vice Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，猶為少府監云。

translations.literal: In the Xiande era of Zhou he was still Vice Director of the Palace Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: As late as Zhou Xiande he still held the post of Vice Director of Palace Manufactories.

sentences.zh: 張文禮者，狡獪人也，镕惑愛之，以為子，號王德明。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenli was a crafty man; Rong favored him, adopted him as a son, and styled him Wang Deming.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenli was cunning. Rong doted on him, adopted him, and gave him the name Wang Deming.

sentences.zh: 镕已死，文禮自為留後。

translations.literal: After Rong died Wenli made himself acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong was dead Wenli declared himself acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 莊宗初納之，後知其通於梁也，遣趙故將符習與閻寶擊之。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong at first accepted him; later learning he was in league with Liang he sent the Zhao veterans Fu Xi and Yan Bao against him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong confirmed him at first, then learned he was dealing with Liang and sent Fu Xi and Yan Bao, old officers of Zhao, to bring him down.

sentences.zh: 文禮家鬼夜哭，野河水變為血，游魚皆死，文禮懼，病疽卒。

translations.literal: Ghosts wept in Wenli’s house by night; the wild river ran blood; fish in the stream died; Wenli was afraid and died of a carbuncle.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits wailed in Wenli’s hall at night; the river outside turned to blood and the fish died. Wenli took fright and died of an abscess.

sentences.zh: 子處瑾秘喪拒守，擊敗習等。

translations.literal: His son Chujin concealed the death and held out; he defeated Fu Xi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chujin hid the corpse and held the city; he beat back Fu Xi’s force.

sentences.zh: 以李嗣昭代之，嗣昭中流矢卒，以李存進代之，存進輒復戰歿，乃以符存審為招討使，遂破之。

translations.literal: Li Sizhao was sent to replace him; Sizhao took an arrow and died. Li Cunjin was sent in his place and immediately fell in battle again. Then Fu Cunshen was made campaign commander and at last broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao was sent to succeed him and died of an arrow wound. Li Cunjin followed and fell in the same fighting. At last Fu Cunshen took command and broke the holdout.

sentences.zh: 執文禮妻及子處瑾、處球、處琪等，折足歸於晉。

translations.literal: They seized Wenli’s wife and his sons Chujin, Chuqiu, and Chuqi, broke their legs, and sent them to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: They captured Wenli’s wife and his sons Chujin, Chuqiu, and Chuqi, shattered their legs, and sent them to Jin.

sentences.zh: 趙人請而醢之，磔文禮屍於市。

translations.literal: The people of Zhao asked permission and pickled them; Wenli’s corpse was dismembered in the market.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao people begged leave to pickle them alive; Wenli’s body was torn apart in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 羅紹威

translations.literal: Luo Shaowei
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shaowei

sentences.zh: 羅紹威，字端己，其先長沙人。

translations.literal: Luo Shaowei, courtesy name Duanyi, was descended from men of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shaowei, courtesy name Duanyi, came of Changsha stock.

sentences.zh: 祖讓，北遷為魏州貴鄉人。

translations.literal: His grandfather Rang moved north and became a man of Guixiang in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Rang migrated north and settled at Guixiang in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 父弘信，為牧監卒。

translations.literal: His father Hongxin had been a herd-overseer’s runner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hongxin had served as a clerk to a pasture inspector.

sentences.zh: 文德元年，魏博牙軍亂，遂殺其帥樂彥貞，立其將趙文建為留後，已而又殺之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wende the Wei Bo guard army mutinied, killed their commander Yue Yanzhen, and set up their general Zhao Wenjian as acting commissioner—then killed him as well.
translations.idiomatic: In Wende 1 the Wei Bo guard mutinied, slew their commissioner Yue Yanzhen, and raised the general Zhao Wenjian—only to kill him in turn.

sentences.zh: 牙將未知所立，乃聚呼曰：「孰能為我帥者？

translations.literal: The guard generals did not know whom to install; they gathered and called out: “Who among you can be our commander?
translations.idiomatic: The guard officers could agree on no one. They assembled and shouted: “Who will lead us?

sentences.zh: 」弘信從眾中出應曰：「我可為君等帥也。

translations.literal: ” Hongxin stepped from the crowd and answered: “I can be commander for you.
translations.idiomatic: ” Hongxin pushed forward from the ranks: “I will be your commander.

sentences.zh: 」弘信狀貌奇怪，面色青黑，軍中異之，共立為留後。

translations.literal: ” Hongxin’s appearance was strange, his face green-black; the army thought him odd and together set him up as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: ” He was a strange-looking man, his face greenish black; the troops marveled and made him acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 唐昭宗即位，拜弘信節度使。

translations.literal: When Tang Zhaozong took the throne he appointed Hongxin military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong came to the throne he confirmed Hongxin as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖將攻晉，乞糴於弘信，弘信不與，由是有隙。

translations.literal: Liang Taizu was about to attack Jin and asked Hongxin for grain; Hongxin refused, and from this a rift opened.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Taizu prepared to strike Jin and asked Hongxin for grain. Hongxin refused, and the breach began.

sentences.zh: 梁兵攻魏，取黎陽、淇門、衛縣。

translations.literal: Liang’s army attacked Wei and took Liyang, Qimen, and Weixian.
translations.idiomatic: Liang marched on Wei and seized Liyang, Qimen, and Weixian.

sentences.zh: 戰於內黃，魏兵五戰五敗，弘信懼，請盟，乃止。

translations.literal: They fought at Neihuang; the Wei army lost five battles in five; Hongxin was afraid, sued for alliance, and the fighting stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At Neihuang the Wei army lost five times in five days. Hongxin sued for peace, and the campaign ended.

sentences.zh: 是時，梁方東攻兗、鄆，北敵晉，晉遣李存信救朱宣，假道於魏。

translations.literal: At that time Liang was attacking Yan and Yun in the east while Jin threatened from the north; Jin sent Li Cunxin to rescue Zhu Xuan and asked passage through Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was fighting east in Yan and Yun while Jin pressed from the north. Jin sent Li Cunxin to save Zhu Xuan and asked to march through Wei.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞，遣使語弘信曰：「晉人志在河朔，兵還滅魏矣。

translations.literal: Taizu heard of it and sent an envoy to tell Hongxin: “The Jin aim at the lands north of the Yellow River. When their army returns it will destroy Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent word to Hongxin: “Jin wants all of Hebei. When they march home they will swallow Wei.

sentences.zh: 」弘信以為然，乃發兵擊存信於莘縣，太祖遣葛從周助之。

translations.literal: Hongxin believed it, sent troops to strike Cunxin at Shenxian, and Taizu sent Ge Congzhou to help.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin believed him, attacked Cunxin at Shenxian, and Taizu sent Ge Congzhou to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 梁兵擒晉王子落落，送於魏，弘信殺之，乃與晉絕。

translations.literal: Liang captured Jin’s prince Luoluo and sent him to Wei; Hongxin killed him and broke with Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Liang took Jin’s prince Luoluo and sent him to Wei. Hongxin executed him and cut ties with Jin.

sentences.zh: 太祖猶疑弘信有二心，乃以兄事弘信，常為卑辭厚幣以聘魏。

translations.literal: Taizu still suspected Hongxin of divided loyalty; he treated him as an elder brother and constantly sent humble words and rich gifts to court him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu still doubted Hongxin’s loyalty. He called him “elder brother,” flattered him, and showered Wei with gifts.

sentences.zh: 魏使者至梁，太祖北面拜而受幣，謂使者曰：「六兄於我有倍年之長，吾何敢慢之。

translations.literal: When a Wei envoy reached Liang, Taizu bowed facing north to receive the gifts and told the envoy: “Sixth Elder is more than a year my senior—how dare I slight him?
translations.idiomatic: When Wei’s envoys came to Liang, Taizu bowed toward the north to accept their gifts and said: “Sixth Elder is a year older than I—how could I treat him lightly?

sentences.zh: 」弘信大喜，以為厚己。

translations.literal: Hongxin was greatly pleased and thought himself honored.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin was delighted and believed himself cherished.

sentences.zh: 以故太祖往來燕、趙之間，卒有河北者，魏不為之患也。

translations.literal: For this reason when Taizu moved between Yan and Zhao and at last held Hebei, Wei gave him no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, when Taizu campaigned between Yan and Zhao and finally took Hebei, Wei never stood in his way.

sentences.zh: 弘信死，紹威立。

translations.literal: Hongxin died; Shaowei succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin died, and Shaowei took his place.

sentences.zh: 紹威好學工書，頗知屬文，聚書數萬卷，開館以延四方之士。

translations.literal: Shaowei loved learning and practiced calligraphy; he knew something of composition, collected tens of thousands of books, and opened a hall to entertain scholars from all quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei studied and wrote well, kept tens of thousands of books, and opened his doors to men of letters from everywhere.

sentences.zh: 弘信在唐，以其先長沙人，故封長沙郡王，紹威襲父爵長沙。

translations.literal: Hongxin in Tang’s time, because his ancestors were Changsha men, was enfeoffed Prince of Changsha; Shaowei inherited his father’s rank of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang, Hongxin’s Changsha ancestry had won him the title Prince of Changsha; Shaowei inherited it.

sentences.zh: 紹威新立，幽州劉仁恭以兵十萬攻魏，屠貝州，紹威求救於梁，大敗燕軍於內黃。

translations.literal: Soon after Shaowei took power, Liu Rengong of Youzhou attacked Wei with a hundred thousand men, slaughtered Beizhou, and Shaowei begged aid from Liang and greatly defeated the Yan army at Neihuang.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after his accession Liu Rengong of Youzhou marched on Wei with a hundred thousand men, sacked Beizhou, and Shaowei called on Liang—who routed the Yan army at Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 明年，梁太祖遣葛從周會魏兵攻滄州，取其德州，遂敗燕軍於老鴉堤，紹威以故德梁助己。

translations.literal: The next year Liang Taizu sent Ge Congzhou with Wei troops to attack Cangzhou, took its Dezhou, and then defeated the Yan army at Laoya Embankment; Shaowei for this reason was deeply grateful to Liang for helping him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Taizu sent Ge Congzhou with Wei’s army against Cangzhou. They took Dezhou and crushed Yan at Laoya Embankment. Shaowei never forgot Liang’s aid.

sentences.zh: 魏博自田承嗣始有牙軍，牙軍歲久益驕，至紹威時已二百年，父子世相婚姻以自結。

translations.literal: Wei Bo since Tian Chengsi had had a guard army; over the years the guard grew ever prouder; by Shaowei’s time it had been two hundred years, and father and son for generations had intermarried to bind themselves together.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bo’s guard corps dated from Tian Chengsi. Century by century it grew more arrogant; by Shaowei’s day it had ruled for two hundred years, its families knit by intermarriage.

sentences.zh: 前帥史憲誠、何全皞、韓君雄、樂彥貞等，皆由牙軍所立，怒輒遂殺之。

translations.literal: Former commanders such as Shi Xiancheng, He Quanhao, Han Junxiong, and Yue Yanzhen had all been set up by the guard; when angered the guard killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioners like Shi Xiancheng, He Quanhao, Han Junxiong, and Yue Yanzhen had all been installed by the guard—and killed by the guard when it pleased.

sentences.zh: 紹威為人精悍明敏，通習吏事，為政有威嚴，然其家世由牙軍所立。

translations.literal: Shaowei was sharp and clear in clerical affairs; his government had authority and sternness—yet his house had been raised by the guard.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei was clever, knew the paperwork, and ruled with a firm hand—yet his own family owed the throne to the guard.

sentences.zh: 天祐二年，魏州城中地陷，紹威懼有變。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianyou the ground sank within Weizhou city; Shaowei feared that change was coming.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou 2 the earth opened in Weizhou. Shaowei feared a reckoning was at hand.

sentences.zh: 已而牙校李公牷作亂，紹威誅之，乃間遣使告梁乞兵，欲盡誅牙軍。

translations.literal: Before long the guard officer Li Gongjun rose in rebellion; Shaowei executed him, then secretly sent envoys to report to Liang and beg troops, intending to exterminate the guard army entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a guard officer named Li Gongjun mutinied; Shaowei put him to death, then sent secret envoys to Liang begging for soldiers—he meant to wipe out the guard army to the last man.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖許之，為遣李思安等攻滄州，召兵於魏，紹威因悉發魏兵以從，獨牙軍在。

translations.literal: Liang Taizu consented and for his part sent Li Si’an and others to attack Cangzhou, summoning troops from Wei; Shaowei therefore sent out all Wei troops to follow, and only the guard army remained.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu agreed and dispatched Li Si’an against Cangzhou, calling up Wei’s levies. Shaowei sent every Wei soldier to march with them, leaving only the guard behind.

sentences.zh: 紹威子廷規娶梁女，會梁女卒，太祖陰遣客將馬嗣勛選良兵實輿中，以長直軍千人雜輿夫入魏，詐為助葬，太祖以兵繼其後。

translations.literal: Shaowei’s son Tinggui had married a Liang princess; when the Liang princess died, Taizu secretly sent his client-general Ma Sixun to select good troops and fill the funeral carts, mixing a thousand long-service troops among the cart-bearers to enter Wei under pretense of aiding the burial; Taizu followed with troops behind.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei’s son Tinggui had married into the Liang house. When the princess died, Taizu secretly sent Ma Sixun to pick elite soldiers and pack them into the funeral train, a thousand veterans disguised as bearers entering Wei to “help with the burial,” with an army close behind.

sentences.zh: 紹威夜以奴兵數百，會嗣勛兵擊牙軍，並其家屬盡殺之。

translations.literal: At night Shaowei led several hundred slave-soldiers, joined Ma Sixun’s troops, and attacked the guard army, killing them together with their families to the last.
translations.idiomatic: That night Shaowei led a few hundred household troops, joined Ma Sixun, and fell on the guard—soldiers and families alike, none left alive.

sentences.zh: 太祖自內黃馳至魏，魏兵從攻滄州者行至歷亭，聞之皆反，入澶、博諸州，魏境大亂，數月，太祖為悉平之。

translations.literal: Taizu galloped from Neihuang to Wei; Wei troops who had gone to attack Cangzhou, reaching Liting, heard the news and all rebelled, entering Chan, Bo, and other prefectures—the Wei realm was in great disorder for months until Taizu personally pacified it all.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu raced from Neihuang to Wei. The Wei detachments bound for Cangzhou heard the news at Liting and turned on their masters, seizing Chan, Bo, and the rest. For months Wei boiled in revolt until Taizu himself beat every faction down.

sentences.zh: 牙軍死，魏兵悉叛，紹威勢益孤，太祖乃欲奪其地，紹威始大悔。

translations.literal: The guard army dead, Wei troops all rebelled; Shaowei’s position grew ever more isolated, and Taizu now wished to seize his territory—Shaowei at last deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: With the guard gone and the field armies in revolt, Shaowei stood alone. Taizu now meant to take his land, and Shaowei saw at last what he had done.

sentences.zh: 是歲，太祖復攻滄州，宿兵長蘆，紹威饋給梁兵，自滄至魏五百里，起亭堠，供帳什物自具，梁兵數十萬皆取足，紹威以此重困。

translations.literal: That year Taizu again attacked Cangzhou and encamped at Changlu; Shaowei supplied the Liang army—from Cang to Wei, five hundred li, he raised beacon towers and furnished lodging and goods himself; several hundred thousand Liang troops all had their fill, and Shaowei was heavily burdened thereby.
translations.idiomatic: That year Taizu besieged Cangzhou again and camped at Changlu. Shaowei fed the Liang host for five hundred li from Cang to Wei—beacon towers, camps, every comfort at his own expense. Hundreds of thousands of Liang mouths ate their fill, and Wei was bled white.

sentences.zh: 昭宗東遷洛陽，詔諸鎮繕理京師，紹威營太廟成，加拜守侍中，進封鄴王。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong moved east to Luoyang, an edict ordered the circuits to repair the capital; Shaowei completed the Imperial Ancestral Temple, was additionally appointed Acting Palace Attendant, and advanced to Prince of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong moved the court to Luoyang, each circuit was told to restore the capital. Shaowei finished the Imperial Ancestral Temple, was made Acting Palace Attendant, and raised to Prince of Ye.

sentences.zh: 燕王劉守光囚其父仁恭，與其兄守文有隙，紹威馳書勸守光等降梁。

translations.literal: The Yan king Liu Shouguang had imprisoned his father Rengong and was at odds with his elder brother Shouwen; Shaowei sent a fast letter urging Shouguang and the others to submit to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan king Liu Shouguang held his father Rengong prisoner and feuded with his brother Shouwen. Shaowei dashed off a letter urging them to surrender to Liang.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之笑曰：「吾常攻燕不能下，今紹威折簡，乃勝用兵十萬。

translations.literal: Taizu heard it and laughed, saying: “I have often attacked Yan without taking it; now Shaowei folds a letter—and that surpasses a hundred thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu laughed when he heard it: “I have hammered at Yan for years without success. Shaowei sends one letter—and that beats an army of a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 」太祖每有大事，多遣使者問之，紹威時亦馳簡入白，使者相遇道中，其事往往相合。

translations.literal: ” Whenever Taizu had a great matter he often sent envoys to ask Shaowei; Shaowei too would rush letters in to report; envoys met one another on the road, and their business often agreed.
translations.idiomatic: ” On every great decision Taizu sent envoys to consult Shaowei; Shaowei rushed his own reports back. Messengers passed one another on the road, and their word usually matched.

sentences.zh: 紹威自以魏久不用兵，願伐木安陽淇門為船，自河入洛，歲漕谷百萬石，以供京師。

translations.literal: Shaowei thought that Wei had long gone without war and wished to cut timber at Anyang and Qimen for boats, enter the river to Luoyang, and each year transport a million piculs of grain to supply the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei thought Wei had been at peace too long. He offered to fell timber at Anyang and Qimen, build boats, sail the Yellow River to Luoyang, and ship a million piculs of grain to the capital every year.

sentences.zh: 太祖益以紹威盡忠，遣將程厚、盧凝督其役。

translations.literal: Taizu all the more took Shaowei for utterly loyal and sent the generals Cheng Hou and Lu Ning to supervise the labor.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu took this as proof of utter loyalty and sent Cheng Hou and Lu Ning to oversee the work.

sentences.zh: 舟未成而紹威病，乃表言：「魏故大鎮，多外兵，願得梁一有功重臣臨之，請以骸骨就第。

translations.literal: Before the boats were finished Shaowei fell ill and memorialized, saying: “Wei is an old great circuit with many outside troops; I wish to have one meritorious, weighty Liang minister come to oversee it; I beg to take my bones home and retire.
translations.idiomatic: The boats were not yet done when Shaowei fell ill. He memorialized: “Wei is a great old circuit, thick with outside troops. Send me a proven Liang minister of rank to hold it—I ask only to go home and die in my bed.

sentences.zh: 」太祖亟命其子周翰監府事，語使者曰：「亟行，語而主，為我強飯，如有不諱，當世世貴爾子孫。

translations.literal: ” Taizu urgently ordered his son Zhouhan to supervise circuit affairs and told the envoy: “Hurry. Tell your lord to eat well for my sake; if the worst comes, I shall ennoble your descendants for generations.
translations.idiomatic: ” Taizu at once put Shaowei’s son Zhouhan in charge of the circuit and told the envoy: “Go quickly. Tell your master to eat for my sake. If he does not recover, his line shall be honored for generations.

sentences.zh: 今使周翰監府事，尚冀卿復愈耳。

translations.literal: Now I have Zhouhan supervise circuit affairs—I still hope you will recover.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouhan holds the circuit for now—I still hope you will rise from this bed.

sentences.zh: 」紹威仕梁，累拜太師兼中書令，卒年三十四，贈尚書令，謚曰貞壯。

translations.literal: ” Serving Liang, Shaowei was repeatedly promoted to Grand Preceptor and Concurrent Chief Councilor; he died at thirty-four, was posthumously made Minister of Works, and given the posthumous name Upright and Strong.
translations.idiomatic: ” Under Liang he rose to Grand Preceptor and Chief Councilor. He died at thirty-four, was posthumously made Minister of Works, and given the posthumous name Zhenzhuang—Upright and Strong.

sentences.zh: 子三人，廷規，官至司農卿卒。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Tinggui, who reached the office of Director of the Imperial Granaries and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons. Tinggui rose to Director of the Imperial Granaries and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 周翰襲父位，乾化二年八月為楊師厚所逐，徙為宣義軍節度使，卒於官，年十四。

translations.literal: Zhouhan inherited his father’s position; in the eighth month of Qianhua 2 he was driven out by Yang Shihou, transferred to military commissioner of the Xuanyi army, and died in office at fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouhan took his father’s seat. In the eighth month of Qianhua 2 Yang Shihou drove him out; he was shifted to Xuanyi commissioner and died in office at fourteen.

sentences.zh: 周敬代為宣義軍節度使，年十歲，徙鎮忠武。

translations.literal: Zhou Jing succeeded him as Xuanyi military commissioner at ten years old, then was transferred to Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jing, ten years old, succeeded him at Xuanyi, then was moved to Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 明年，為秘書監、駙馬都尉、光祿卿。

translations.literal: The next year he was made Director of the Secretariat, Chief Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law, and Minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became Director of the Secretariat, chief commandant of the imperial sons-in-law, and Minister of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗時為金吾大將軍，明宗以為匡國軍節度使，罷為上將軍。

translations.literal: Under Tang Zhuangzong he was made Grand General of the Golden Guards; Mingzong made him military commissioner of the Kuangguo army, then relieved him to serve as Senior General.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhuangzong he was Grand General of the Golden Guards; Mingzong made him Kuangguo commissioner, then retired him to Senior General.

sentences.zh: 晉天福二年卒，年三十二。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianfu of Jin he died at thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jin Tianfu 2, aged thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 廷規娶梁太祖二女，一曰安陽公主，一曰金華公主。

translations.literal: Tinggui married two daughters of Liang Taizu: one the Princess of Anyang, one the Princess of Jinhua.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui married two of Taizu’s daughters—the Princesses of Anyang and Jinhua.

sentences.zh: 周翰娶末帝女，曰壽春公主，周敬亦娶末帝女，曰晉安公主。

translations.literal: Zhouhan married a daughter of the Last Emperor, the Princess of Shouchun; Zhou Jing also married a daughter of the Last Emperor, the Princess of Jin’an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouhan married the Last Emperor’s daughter, the Princess of Shouchun; Zhou Jing married his sister, the Princess of Jin’an.

sentences.zh: 王處直

translations.literal: Wang Chuzhi
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chuzhi

sentences.zh: 王處直，字允明，京兆萬年人也。

translations.literal: Wang Chuzhi, courtesy name Yunming, was a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chuzhi, courtesy name Yunming, came from Wannian in the capital district.

sentences.zh: 父宗，善殖財貨，富擬王侯，為唐神策軍吏，官至金吾大將軍，領興元節度使，子處存、處直。

translations.literal: His father Zong was skilled at amassing wealth; his riches rivaled kings and marquises. He was an officer of the Tang Shence Army, rose to Grand General of the Golden Guards and held the post of military commissioner of Xingyuan, and had sons Chucun and Chuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zong knew how to pile up money until his wealth rivaled princes. He served in the Shence Army, rose to Grand General of the Golden Guards and commissioner of Xingyuan, and fathered Chucun and Chuzhi.

sentences.zh: 處存以父任為驍衛將軍、定州已來制置內閑廄宮苑等使。

translations.literal: Chucun, through his father’s position, became a general of the Valiant Guards and commissioner for the inner stables, palace parks, and related offices from Dingzhou southward.
translations.idiomatic: Chucun inherited his father’s favor and became a Valiant Guard general and commissioner over the inner stables and palace parks from Dingzhou south.

sentences.zh: 乾符六年，即拜義武軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Ganfu he was at once appointed military commissioner of the Yiwu army.
translations.idiomatic: In Ganfu 6 he was appointed military commissioner of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 黃巢陷長安，處存感憤流涕，率鎮兵入關討賊。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao took Chang’an, Chucun, moved to tears, led his circuit troops into the passes to attack the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao seized Chang’an, Chucun wept with rage and led his troops through the passes against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 巢敗第功，而收城擊賊，李克用為第一；

translations.literal: When the nest was broken merit was ranked: in retaking the city and striking the bandits, Li Keyong was first;
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were broken, rewards were tallied. For retaking the city and striking the bandits, Li Keyong ranked first;

sentences.zh: 勤王倡義，處存為第一。

translations.literal: in rallying loyal troops and raising righteous arms, Chucun was first.
translations.idiomatic: for rallying loyal troops and raising the righteous standard, Chucun ranked first.

sentences.zh: 乾寧二年，處存卒於鎮，三軍以河朔故事，推處存子郜為留後，即拜節度使，加檢校司空、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianning Chucun died in the circuit; the three armies, following the Hebei custom, pushed Chucun’s son Gao as acting commissioner; he was at once appointed military commissioner and additionally made Acting Minister of Works and Concurrent Chief Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianning 2 Chucun died at his post. The army, by Hebei custom, made his son Gao acting commissioner; the court confirmed him, added Acting Minister of Works and Chief Councilor.

sentences.zh: 處直為後院中軍都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: Chuzhi was commander of the rear courtyard’s central army, knowing troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi commanded the rear courtyard’s central army.

sentences.zh: 處直好巫，而客有李應之者，妖妄人也。

translations.literal: Chuzhi was fond of shamans; among his clients was Li Yingzhi, a man of delusion and falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi doted on shamans. Among his hangers-on was Li Yingzhi, a fraud and a charlatan.

sentences.zh: 處直有疾，應之以左道治之而愈，處直益以為神，使衣道士服，以為行營司馬，軍政無大小，咸取決焉。

translations.literal: When Chuzhi fell ill, Yingzhi treated him by heterodox ways and he recovered; Chuzhi all the more took him for divine, had him wear Taoist robes, and made him camp marshal of the mobile headquarters; great and small in military affairs all were decided by him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuzhi fell ill, Yingzhi cured him with forbidden rites. Chuzhi then called him a god, dressed him as a Taoist, made him camp marshal, and let him rule every military decision, large or small.

sentences.zh: 初，應之於陘邑闌得小兒劉雲郎，養以為子，而處直未有子，乃以雲郎與處直，而紿曰：「此子生而有異。

translations.literal: Earlier Yingzhi had snatched up a small boy, Liu Yunlang, at a barrier in Xingyi and raised him as a son; Chuzhi had no son, so he gave Yunlang to Chuzhi and deceived him, saying: “This child was born with wonders.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhi had once taken a boy named Liu Yunlang from a Xingyi barrier and raised him. Chuzhi had no heir, so Yingzhi presented the boy and lied: “This child was born under strange signs.

sentences.zh: 」處直養以為子，更名曰都，甚愛之。

translations.literal: ” Chuzhi raised him as a son, changed his name to Du, and loved him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chuzhi adopted him, renamed him Du, and loved him like his own blood.

sentences.zh: 應之由此益橫，乃籍管內丁壯，別立新軍，自將之，治第博陵坊，四面開門，皆用左道。

translations.literal: From this Yingzhi grew ever more overbearing; he registered able-bodied men within the circuit, formed a new army under his own command, built a mansion in Boling Ward with gates on all four sides, and used heterodox ways throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhi grew insolent. He levied every able man in the circuit, raised a private army, built a mansion in Boling Ward with gates on every side, and filled it with sorcery.

sentences.zh: 處直將吏知其必為患，而莫能諫也。

translations.literal: Chuzhi’s officers and clerks knew he would surely bring disaster, yet none could remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi’s officers saw the disaster coming and could not make him listen.

sentences.zh: 是時，幽州李匡儔假道中山以如京師，處直伏甲城外，以備不虞。

translations.literal: At that time Li Kuangchou of Youzhou asked passage through Zhongshan on his way to the capital; Chuzhi hid armed men outside the walls against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuangchou of Youzhou asked to march through Zhongshan on his way to court. Chuzhi hid troops outside the walls, fearing treachery.

sentences.zh: 匡儔已去，甲士入城圍應之第，執而殺之，因詣處直請殺都，處直不與。

translations.literal: Kuangchou had already gone; the armed men entered the city, surrounded Yingzhi’s mansion, seized and killed him, then went to Chuzhi to ask that Du be killed too—Chuzhi would not give him up.
translations.idiomatic: Once Kuangchou had passed, the soldiers entered the city, besieged Yingzhi’s house, and killed him. They then begged Chuzhi to kill Du as well. He refused.

sentences.zh: 明日，第功行賞，因陰疏甲士姓名，自隊長已上藏於別籍，其後因事誅之，凡二十年，無一人免者，而處直終為都所殺。

translations.literal: The next day, when merit was ranked and rewards given, he secretly listed the armed men’s names from squad leaders upward in a separate register; afterward he killed them on one pretext or another—for twenty years not one escaped, yet in the end Chuzhi was killed by Du.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he handed out rewards—and quietly copied every soldier’s name from squad leader up into a secret roll. For twenty years he killed them one by one, never sparing a man. In the end Du killed him anyway.

sentences.zh: 都為人狡佞多謀，處直以為節度副使。

translations.literal: Du was crafty, fawning, and full of schemes; Chuzhi made him deputy military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Du was sly, flattering, and scheming. Chuzhi made him deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 張文禮弒王镕，莊宗發兵討文禮，處直與左右謀曰：「鎮，定之蔽也，文禮雖有罪，然鎮亡定不獨存。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenli murdered Wang Rong; Zhuangzong raised troops to punish Wenli. Chuzhi consulted his close advisers, saying: “Zhen and Ding shield each other; though Wenli is guilty, if Zhen perishes Ding cannot stand alone.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenli murdered Wang Rong, and Zhuangzong marched to punish him. Chuzhi told his intimates: “Zhen and Ding are one shield. Wenli may be guilty, but if Zhen falls, Ding cannot stand alone.

sentences.zh: 」乃遣人請莊宗毋發兵，莊宗取所獲文禮與梁蠟書示處直曰：「文禮負我，師不可止。

translations.literal: ” He sent men to ask Zhuangzong not to march; Zhuangzong took the captured letters between Wenli and Liang sealed in wax and showed Chuzhi, saying: “Wenli has betrayed me—the army cannot stop.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sent envoys begging Zhuangzong to stay his hand. Zhuangzong showed him the wax-sealed letters Wenli had sent Liang: “Wenli has betrayed me. The campaign does not stop.

sentences.zh: 」處直有孽子郁，當郜之亡於晉也，郁亦奔焉，晉王以女妻之，為新州防禦使。

translations.literal: ” Chuzhi had a bastard son Yu; when Gao was lost to Jin, Yu had fled there too; the Prince of Jin gave him a daughter in marriage and made him defender of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chuzhi had a bastard son, Yu. When Gao fell to Jin, Yu fled there as well; the Prince of Jin gave him a princess and made him defender of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 處直見莊宗必討文禮，益自疑，乃陰與郁交通，使郁北招契丹入塞以牽晉兵，且許召郁為嗣，都聞之不說。

translations.literal: Seeing that Zhuangzong would surely punish Wenli, Chuzhi grew all the more suspicious and secretly communicated with Yu, having Yu summon the Khitan north of the passes to raid and tie down Jin’s troops; he also promised to call Yu back as heir. When Du heard it he was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Zhuangzong would not relent, Chuzhi grew afraid and wrote secretly to Yu, telling him to bring the Khitan across the border to pin Jin’s armies, and promised to name him heir. Du was not pleased.

sentences.zh: 而定人皆言契丹不可召，恐自貽患，處直不聽。

translations.literal: Yet the people of Ding all said the Khitan must not be summoned, lest they bring disaster on themselves—Chuzhi would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in Ding said the same: do not call the Khitan, or you invite ruin. Chuzhi would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 郁自奔晉，常恐處直不容，因此大喜，以為乘其隙可取之，乃以厚賂誘契丹阿保機。

translations.literal: Yu, having fled to Jin, always feared Chuzhi would not spare him; he therefore rejoiced greatly, thinking that in this gap he could seize the circuit; he used rich bribes to entice the Khitan Abaoji.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had fled to Jin and always feared Chuzhi would never forgive him. Now he rejoiced, thinking the moment ripe to take Ding, and bribed Abaoji of the Khitan with heavy gifts.

sentences.zh: 阿保機舉國入寇，定人皆不欲契丹之舉，小吏和昭訓勸都舉事，都因執處直，囚之西宅，自為留後，凡王氏子孫及處直將校殺戮殆盡。

translations.literal: Abaoji led his whole nation in invasion; the people of Ding all did not want the Khitan’s action. The petty clerk He Zhaoxun urged Du to act; Du therefore seized Chuzhi, imprisoned him in the western residence, and made himself acting commissioner, slaughtering nearly all the Wang clan and Chuzhi’s officers.
translations.idiomatic: Abaoji invaded with the whole Khitan nation. Ding wanted no part of it. A clerk named He Zhaoxun urged Du to strike. Du seized Chuzhi, locked him in the west hall, declared himself acting commissioner, and butchered nearly every Wang and every loyal officer.

sentences.zh: 明年正月朔旦，都拜處直於西宅，處直奮起揕其胸而呼曰：「逆賊！

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the next year Du had Chuzhi bow to him in the western residence; Chuzhi roused himself and stabbed at his chest, crying: “Rebel!
translations.idiomatic: On New Year’s morning Du made Chuzhi bow to him in the west hall. Chuzhi lunged up and drove at his chest, shouting, “Traitor!

sentences.zh: 吾何負爾？

translations.literal: What have I done to wrong you?
translations.idiomatic: What wrong did I ever do you?

sentences.zh: 」然左右無兵，遂欲嚙其鼻，都掣袖而走，處直遂見殺。

translations.literal: ” But those at hand had no weapons; he then tried to bite off Du’s nose; Du pulled his sleeve free and fled—Chuzhi was thereupon killed.
translations.idiomatic: ” He had no weapon but his teeth and tried to tear Du’s nose off. Du wrenched free and ran. They killed Chuzhi where he stood.

sentences.zh: 初，有黃蛇見於碑樓，處直以為龍，藏而祠之，又有野鵲數百，巢麥田中，處直以為己德所致，而定人皆知其不祥，曰：「蛇穴山澤，而處人室，鵲巢烏，降而田居，小人竊位，而在上者失其所居之象也。

translations.literal: Earlier a yellow snake had appeared at the tablet tower; Chuzhi took it for a dragon, hid it and made offerings; again several hundred wild magpies nested in the wheat fields—Chuzhi took this as virtue he had brought about, but the people of Ding all knew it was inauspicious, saying: “Snakes dwell in hills and marshes, yet this one entered a human house; magpies nest in trees, yet these descended to the fields—a petty man steals rank, and those above lose their place—that is the omen.
translations.idiomatic: A yellow snake had once appeared at the tablet tower; Chuzhi called it a dragon, hid it, and worshipped it. Hundreds of magpies nested in the wheat—Chuzhi took that as proof of his virtue. The people of Ding knew better and said: “Snakes belong in the hills, not in a man’s hall. Magpies belong in trees, not in the grain. A thief climbs high while his betters lose their seat—that is what heaven is showing you.

sentences.zh: 」已而處直果被廢死。

translations.literal: ” Before long Chuzhi was indeed deposed and killed.
translations.idiomatic: ” Soon enough Chuzhi was overthrown and killed.

sentences.zh: 莊宗已敗契丹於沙河，追奔過定州，與都相得歡甚，以其子繼岌娶都女，以都為義武軍節度使。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong had already defeated the Khitan at Shahe; pursuing the rout he passed Dingzhou and got on famously with Du, marrying his son Jiji to Du’s daughter and making Du military commissioner of the Yiwu army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong had beaten the Khitan at Shahe and, chasing the rout, came to Dingzhou. He and Du took to each other at once. He married his son Jiji to Du’s daughter and confirmed Du as Yiwu commissioner.

sentences.zh: 同光二年，莊宗幸鄴，都來朝，賜與巨萬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongguang Zhuangzong visited Ye; Du came to court and was given gifts worth tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongguang 2 Zhuangzong visited Ye. Du came to court and received gifts worth tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 莊宗以繼岌故，待都甚厚，所請無不從。

translations.literal: Because of Jiji, Zhuangzong treated Du very generously; whatever he asked was granted.
translations.idiomatic: For Jiji’s sake Zhuangzong indulged him; Du’s every request was granted.

sentences.zh: 及明宗立，頗惡都為人，而安重誨每以法繩之，都始有異志。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he greatly disliked Du’s character, and An Chonghui constantly held him to the law; Du first harbored other designs.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong despised Du’s character. An Chonghui bound him with regulations. Du began to dream of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 是時，唐兵擊契丹，數往來定州，都供饋多闕，益不自安。

translations.literal: At that time Tang troops attacked the Khitan and passed through Dingzhou again and again; Du’s supplies were often short, and he grew all the more uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: Tang armies marched against the Khitan and passed through Ding again and again. Du could not feed them properly and grew afraid.

sentences.zh: 和昭訓為都謀曰：「天子新立，四方未附，其勢易離，可為自安之計。

translations.literal: He Zhaoxun plotted for Du, saying: “The Son of Heaven has just taken the throne; the four quarters are not yet attached—their position is easy to split. You can plan for your own security.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhaoxun whispered to him: “The throne is new. The realm is not yet bound to it. The court can be broken. You should save yourself while you can.

sentences.zh: 」已而朱守殷反於汴州，都遂亦反，遣人以蠟書招青、徐、岐、潞、梓五鎮，約皆舉兵，而五鎮不應。

translations.literal: ” Before long Zhu Shouyin rebelled at Bianzhou; Du then rebelled too, sending men with wax-sealed letters to summon Qing, Xu, Qi, Lu, and Zi—five circuits—agreeing that all should raise troops, but the five circuits did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: ” Soon Zhu Shouyin rose at Bianzhou. Du rose too, sending wax-sealed letters to Qing, Xu, Qi, Lu, and Zi, calling on five circuits to rebel together. None answered.

sentences.zh: 明宗遣王晏球討之。

translations.literal: Mingzong sent Wang Yanqiu to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong sent Wang Yanqiu against him.

sentences.zh: 都復與王郁招契丹為援，契丹遣禿餒將萬騎救都。

translations.literal: Du again joined Wang Yu in summoning Khitan aid; the Khitan sent Tuyu with ten thousand horsemen to rescue Du.
translations.idiomatic: Du again joined Wang Yu in calling the Khitan. Tuyu came with ten thousand horsemen to save him.

sentences.zh: 都遣指揮使鄭季璘、龍泉鎮將杜弘壽以二千人迎契丹，為晏球所敗。

translations.literal: Du sent the commander Zheng Jilin and the Longquan garrison commander Du Hongshou with two thousand men to meet the Khitan; Yanqiu defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Du sent Zheng Jilin and the Longquan commander Du Hongshou with two thousand men to meet the Khitan. Yanqiu crushed them.

sentences.zh: 季璘、弘壽被執，晏球責曰：「吾嘗使人招汝，何故不降？

translations.literal: Jilin and Hongshou were captured; Yanqiu reproached them, saying: “I once sent men to summon you—why did you not surrender?
translations.idiomatic: Jilin and Hongshou were taken. Yanqiu demanded: “I sent envoys offering terms. Why did you refuse?

sentences.zh: 」弘壽對曰：「受恩中山兩世矣，不敢有二心。

translations.literal: ” Hongshou replied: “I have received favor from Zhongshan for two generations—I dare not harbor a second heart.
translations.idiomatic: ” Hongshou answered: “Zhongshan favored me for two reigns. I could not betray it.

sentences.zh: 」遂見殺，弘壽臨刑，神色自若。

translations.literal: ” He was thereupon killed; facing execution Hongshou’s expression was calm.
translations.idiomatic: ” They killed him. Hongshou went to the block without flinching.

sentences.zh: 晏球屯軍望都，與都及契丹戰，大敗之曲陽，都及禿餒得數騎遁去，閉城不復出。

translations.literal: Yanqiu encamped at Wangdu and fought Du and the Khitan, routing them badly at Quyang; Du and Tuyu escaped with a few horsemen, shut the city, and did not come out again.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqiu camped at Wangdu and met Du and the Khitan at Quyang, breaking them utterly. Du and Tuyu fled with a handful of riders, barred the gates, and would not come out again.

sentences.zh: 初，處直為都所囚，幼子威北走契丹。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chuzhi was imprisoned by Du, his young son Wei fled north to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: When Du seized Chuzhi, his young son Wei fled north to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 契丹謂晉高祖曰：「吾欲使威襲其先人爵士，如何？

translations.literal: The Khitan said to Jin Gaozu: “I wish to have Wei recover his forefathers’ fief—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan asked Jin Gaozu: “Let Wei take back his family’s circuit. What say you?

sentences.zh: 」高祖對曰：「中國之法，自將校為刺史，升團練防禦而至節度使，請送威歸中國，漸進之。

translations.literal: ” Gaozu replied: “By the law of the Central Realm, from regimental officer one rises to prefect, then to regimental training commissioner and defense commissioner, and only then to military commissioner—please send Wei back to the Central Realm and advance him step by step.
translations.idiomatic: ” Gaozu answered: “By Central Realm custom a man rises from regimental officer to prefect, then to training commissioner and defender, and only then to military commissioner. Send Wei home and promote him in due order.

sentences.zh: 」契丹怒曰：「爾自諸侯為天子，豈有漸乎？

translations.literal: ” The Khitan angrily said: “You yourself went from feudal lord to Son of Heaven—is there such a thing as step by step?
translations.idiomatic: ” The Khitan snapped: “You went from warlord to Son of Heaven overnight. Where is your ‘step by step’?

sentences.zh: 」高祖聞之，遽徙廷胤鎮義武，曰：「此亦王氏之後也。

translations.literal: ” Hearing this, Gaozu hastily transferred Tingyin to Yiwu, saying: “He too is a descendant of the Wang house.
translations.idiomatic: ” Alarmed, Gaozu at once moved Tingyin to Yiwu, saying: “He is Wang blood as well.

sentences.zh: 」後徙鎮海而卒。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Zhenhai and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was shifted to Zhenhai and died there.

sentences.zh: 劉守光

translations.literal: Liu Shouguang
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shouguang

sentences.zh: 劉守光，深州樂壽人也。

translations.literal: Liu Shouguang was a man of Leshou in Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shouguang came from Leshou in Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 其父仁恭，事幽州李可舉，能穴地為道以攻城，軍中號「劉窟頭。

translations.literal: His father Rengong served Li Keju of Youzhou and could dig underground passages to take cities; in the army he was called “Liu the Burrower.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rengong served Li Keju of Youzhou and could mine tunnels under city walls; the troops called him “Liu the Burrower.

sentences.zh: 」稍以功遷軍校。

translations.literal: ” He gradually rose by merit to army officer.
translations.idiomatic: ” He rose by merit to army officer.

sentences.zh: 仁恭為人有勇，好大言。

translations.literal: Rengong was a man of courage who loved grand talk.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong was brave and loved to boast.

sentences.zh: 可舉死，子匡威惡其為人，不欲使居軍中，徙為瀛州景城縣令。

translations.literal: When Keju died, his son Kuangwei disliked Rengong’s character and did not wish to keep him in the army, transferring him to be magistrate of Jingcheng county in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Keju died, his son Kuangwei disliked Rengong and pushed him out of the army, making him magistrate of Jingcheng in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 瀛州軍亂，殺刺史，仁恭募縣中得千人，討平之，匡威喜，復以為將，使戍蔚州。

translations.literal: Yingzhou’s army mutinied and killed the prefect; Rengong recruited a thousand men from the county, suppressed the disorder, and Kuangwei was pleased and again made him a general, sending him to garrison Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Yingzhou garrison mutinied and killed the prefect. Rengong raised a thousand county men, put the mutiny down, and Kuangwei was so pleased he made him a general again and sent him to garrison Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 戍兵過期不得代，皆思歸，出怨言。

translations.literal: The garrison troops passed their term without relief and all longed to return, voicing complaints.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison’s term expired with no relief in sight. The men grumbled and yearned for home.

sentences.zh: 匡威為弟匡儔所逐，仁恭聞亂，乃擁戍兵攻幽州，行至居庸關，戰敗，奔晉、晉以為壽陽鎮將。

translations.literal: Kuangwei was driven out by his younger brother Kuangchou; hearing of the disorder, Rengong led the garrison troops to attack Youzhou, reached Juyong Pass, was defeated in battle, fled to Jin, and Jin made him defender of Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangchou drove Kuangwei out. Rengong heard of the chaos, led his garrison against Youzhou, was beaten at Juyong Pass, fled to Jin, and Jin made him defender of Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 仁恭父子率兩鎮兵十萬，號稱三十萬以擊魏，屠貝州。

translations.literal: Father and sons led a hundred thousand men from the two circuits, claiming three hundred thousand, to attack Wei and slaughtered Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Father and sons marched a hundred thousand men from two circuits—they claimed three hundred thousand—against Wei and sacked Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 羅紹威求救於梁，梁遣李思安救魏，大敗守文於內黃，斬首五萬。

translations.literal: Luo Shaowei begged Liang for rescue; Liang sent Li Si’an to save Wei and utterly defeated Shouwen at Neihuang, beheading fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shaowei begged Liang for aid. Liang sent Li Si’an to relieve Wei and shattered Shouwen at Neihuang, taking fifty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 仁恭走，梁軍追擊之，自魏至長河，橫屍數百里。

translations.literal: Rengong fled; the Liang army pursued from Wei to Changhe—corpses lay across hundreds of li.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong fled. The Liang pursuers chased from Wei to Changhe until the road was carpeted with dead for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 梁軍自是連歲攻之，破其瀛、漠二州，仁恭懼，復附晉。

translations.literal: The Liang army thereafter attacked year after year, took his Ying and Mo prefectures, and Rengong in fear again submitted to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Liang attacked year after year, took Ying and Mo, and Rengong, afraid, submitted to Jin again.

sentences.zh: 天祐三年，梁攻滄州，仁恭調其境內凡男子年十五已上、七十已下，皆黥其面，文曰「定霸都」，得二十萬人，兵糧自具，屯於瓦橋。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianyou Liang attacked Cangzhou; Rengong mobilized every man in his territory from fifteen up and seventy down, tattooed their faces with the characters “Settling the Hegemon’s Capital,” mustered two hundred thousand men who brought their own grain and weapons, and encamped at Waqiao.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou 3 Liang besieged Cangzhou. Rengong called up every male from fifteen to seventy, branded their faces with “Settling the Hegemon’s Capital,” and raised two hundred thousand men who fed and armed themselves, camping at Waqiao.

sentences.zh: 梁軍壁長蘆，深溝高壘，仁恭不能近。

translations.literal: The Liang army walled at Changlu with deep ditches and high ramparts; Rengong could not approach.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang host dug in at Changlu behind deep trenches and high walls. Rengong could not reach them.

sentences.zh: 滄州被圍百餘日，城中食盡，人自相食，析骸而爨，或丸墐土而食，死者十六七。

translations.literal: Cangzhou was besieged more than a hundred days; food in the city was exhausted and men ate one another, breaking bones to cook, or rolled clay into balls to eat—six or seven in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: Cangzhou starved for more than a hundred days. Men ate one another, boiled bones for broth, kneaded clay into balls to swallow. Six or seven in ten died.

sentences.zh: 仁恭求救於晉，晉王為之攻潞州以牽梁圍，晉破潞州，梁軍乃解去。

translations.literal: Rengong begged Jin for rescue; the Prince of Jin for his sake attacked Luzhou to draw off the Liang siege; Jin took Luzhou and the Liang army then lifted the siege and left.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong begged Jin for help. The Prince of Jin struck Luzhou to pull Liang away. Jin took Luzhou, and the siege broke.

sentences.zh: 然仁恭幸世多故，而驕於富貴，築宮大安山，窮極奢侈，選燕美女充其中。

translations.literal: Yet Rengong, trusting that the age brought many troubles, grew arrogant in wealth; he built a palace on Mount Da’an of utmost extravagance and chose the beauties of Yan to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong trusted chaos to protect him and swaggered in his riches. He built a palace on Mount Da’an of impossible luxury and stocked it with Yan’s fairest women.

sentences.zh: 又與道士煉丹藥，冀可不死。

translations.literal: He also refined elixirs with Taoists, hoping he might not die.
translations.idiomatic: He brewed elixirs with Taoist priests, hoping never to die.

sentences.zh: 令燕人用墐土為錢，悉斂銅錢，鑾山而藏之，已而殺其工以滅口，後人皆莫知其處。

translations.literal: He ordered the people of Yan to use clay for coin, collected all copper cash, mined a mountain to hide it, then killed the workmen to silence them—later men never knew the place.
translations.idiomatic: He forced Yan to use clay coins, seized every copper cash, mined a mountain to bury the hoard, then killed the laborers to seal the secret. No one ever found it again.

sentences.zh: 仁恭有愛妾羅氏，其子守光烝之，仁恭怒，笞守光，逐之。

translations.literal: Rengong had a favorite concubine, Lady Luo; his son Shouguang violated her; Rengong in anger flogged Shouguang and drove him out.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong kept a favorite, Lady Luo. His son Shouguang took her. Rengong beat him and cast him out.

sentences.zh: 梁開平元年，遣李思安攻仁恭，仁恭在大安，守光自外將兵以入，擊走思安，乃自稱盧龍節度使，遣李小喜、元行欽以兵攻大安山，執仁恭而幽之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiping Liang sent Li Si’an to attack Rengong; Rengong was on Mount Da’an; Shouguang led troops in from outside, struck and drove off Si’an, then declared himself military commissioner of Lulong, sent Li Xiaoxi and Yuan Xingqin with troops to attack Mount Da’an, seized Rengong, and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiping 1 Liang sent Li Si’an against Rengong, who was on Mount Da’an. Shouguang marched in from outside, routed Si’an, named himself Lulong commissioner, and sent Li Xiaoxi and Yuan Xingqin to take Mount Da’an, seize Rengong, and lock him away.

sentences.zh: 其兄守文聞父且囚，即率兵討守光，至於盧臺，為守光所敗，進戰玉田，又敗，乃乞兵於契丹。

translations.literal: His elder brother Shouwen heard their father was about to be imprisoned and at once led troops to punish Shouguang; reaching Lutai he was defeated by Shouguang; advancing to fight at Yutian he was defeated again, and then begged troops from the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Shouwen heard their father was taken and marched to punish Shouguang. At Lutai Shouguang broke him; at Yutian he broke him again. Shouwen turned to the Khitan for soldiers.

sentences.zh: 明年，守文將契丹、吐渾兵四萬人戰於雞蘇，守光兵敗，守文陽為不忍，出於陣而呼其眾曰：「毋殺吾弟！

translations.literal: The next year Shouwen led forty thousand Khitan and Tuhun troops to battle at Jisu; Shouguang’s army was defeated. Shouwen feigned pity, came out before the ranks, and called to his troops: “Do not kill my younger brother!
translations.idiomatic: The following year Shouwen marched forty thousand Khitan and Tuhun troops to Jisu. Shouguang was routed. Shouwen made a show of mercy, rode out before the lines, and cried to his men: “Spare my brother!

sentences.zh: 」守光將元行欽識守文，躍馬而擒之，又囚之於別室，既而殺之。

translations.literal: ” Shouguang’s general Yuan Xingqin recognized Shouwen, spurred his horse, seized him, and imprisoned him in another room; soon after he killed him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yuan Xingqin, a Shouguang general who knew Shouwen by sight, charged, pulled him from the saddle, and shut him in a side room—then killed him.

sentences.zh: 守文將吏孫鶴、呂兗等，立守文子延祚以距守光，守光圍之百餘日，城中食盡，米斛直錢三萬，人相殺而食，或食墐土，馬相食其駿尾，兗等率城中饑民食以麹，號「宰務」，日殺以餉軍。

translations.literal: Shouwen’s officers Sun He, Lu Yan, and others set up Shouwen’s son Yanzuo to resist Shouguang. Shouguang besieged them for more than a hundred days. Food in the city ran out; a peck of rice cost thirty thousand cash. Men killed one another to eat, or ate plastered earth; horses ate one another’s tails. Yan and the rest fed the starving townspeople leaven, calling it “Slaughter Duty”—each day they killed people to provision the army.
translations.idiomatic: Sun He, Lu Yan, and Shouwen’s other officers put his son Yanzuo on the throne to hold Shouguang off. The siege lasted more than a hundred days. Grain failed; a peck of rice fetched thirty thousand cash. Men butchered one another for meat, or gnawed plaster from the walls; horses ate the tails of the finer stock. Yan and his fellows fed the starving with fermented mash in what they called “Slaughter Duty”—daily killings to keep the garrison fed.

sentences.zh: 久之，延祚力窮，遂降。

translations.literal: After a long time Yanzuo’s strength was exhausted and he surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At last Yanzuo had nothing left and opened the gates.

sentences.zh: 守光素庸愚，由此益驕，為鐵籠、鐵刷，人有過者，坐之籠中，外燎以火，或刷剔其皮膚以死，燕之士逃禍於佗境。

translations.literal: Shouguang had always been dull and foolish; from this he grew still more arrogant. He made iron cages and iron brushes; when anyone faulted, he seated them in the cage and burned fire outside, or scraped the skin from their bodies until they died. Men of Yan fled to other lands to escape disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Shouguang had never been bright; victory only swelled his pride. He built iron cages and iron brushes—offenders were locked in the cage while fire was lit outside, or their skin was scraped away until they died. The gentry of Yan fled across the borders to escape him.

sentences.zh: 守光身衣赭黃，謂其將吏曰：「我衣此而南面，可以帝天下乎？

translations.literal: Shouguang himself wore ochre-yellow robes and said to his officers: “If I wear this and face south, can I be emperor of all under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Shouguang dressed himself in imperial ochre-yellow and asked his commanders: “Clothed like this and facing south, could I not rule the realm?

sentences.zh: 」孫鶴切諫以為不可。

translations.literal: ” Sun He urgently remonstrated that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: ” Sun He pleaded with him to abandon the thought.

sentences.zh: 梁攻趙，趙王王镕求救於守光，孫鶴曰：「今趙無罪，而梁伐之，諸侯救趙之兵，先至者霸，臣恐燕軍未出，而晉已先破梁矣，此不可失之時也。

translations.literal: Liang attacked Zhao. Zhao king Wang Rong begged Shouguang for rescue. Sun He said: “Now Zhao is without guilt, yet Liang attacks her. Among the lords, whoever reaches Zhao first to save her will hold the hegemony. I fear before Yan’s army goes out, Jin will already have broken Liang—this is a moment not to be lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang struck Zhao, Wang Rong of Zhao begged Shouguang for aid. Sun He said: “Zhao has done no wrong, yet Liang invades. Among the warlords, the first to rescue her will take the lead. I fear Jin will break Liang before our columns even march—this chance will not come again.

sentences.zh: 」守光曰：「趙王嘗與我盟而背之，今急乃來歸我；

translations.literal: ” Shouguang said: “The Zhao king once allied with me and then turned his back; now in extremity he comes to submit to me;
translations.idiomatic: ” Shouguang replied: “Wang Rong swore alliance with me and broke it; only now, desperate, does he crawl back.

sentences.zh: 且兩虎方鬥，可待之，吾當為卞莊子也。

translations.literal: Besides, two tigers are just now fighting—we may wait. I shall play Bian Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, two tigers are already at each other’s throats. Let them fight. I mean to play Bian Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 」遂不出兵。

translations.literal: ” So he did not send troops.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sent no troops.

sentences.zh: 晉王果救趙，大敗梁兵於柏鄉，進掠邢、洺，至於黎陽。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin indeed rescued Zhao, greatly defeated Liang at Boxiang, advanced to plunder Xing and Mo, and reached Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin did rescue Zhao, crushing Liang at Boxiang, then raiding through Xing and Mo as far as Liyang.

sentences.zh: 守光聞晉空國深入梁，乃治兵戒嚴，遣人以語動鎮、定曰：「燕有精兵三十萬，率二鎮以從晉，然誰當主此盟者？

translations.literal: Shouguang heard Jin had emptied its state and penetrated deep into Liang; then he drilled troops and set strict guard, and sent someone with words to move Zhen and Ding: “Yan has thirty thousand elite troops. I shall lead the two circuits to follow Jin—yet who shall head this alliance?
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Jin had stripped its home garrisons and plunged deep into Liang, Shouguang mustered his army, tightened discipline, and sent envoys to Zhen and Ding: “Yan can field thirty thousand picked men. I will march with your two circuits in Jin’s wake—but who leads this alliance?

sentences.zh: 」晉人患之，謀曰：「昔夫差爭黃池之會，而越入吳；

translations.literal: ” The Jin men were troubled. They consulted: “In ancient times Fuchai contested the meeting at Huangchi and Yue entered Wu;
translations.idiomatic: ” Jin was alarmed. Its officers said: “Long ago Fuchai raced for precedence at Huangchi—and Yue walked into Wu.

sentences.zh: 項羽貪伐齊之利，而漢敗楚。

translations.literal: Xiang Yu grasped at gain in attacking Qi and Han defeated Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu chased profit against Qi, and Han broke Chu.

sentences.zh: 今吾越千里以伐人，而強燕在其後，此腹心之患也。
