translations.literal: Now we march a thousand li to attack another while strong Yan is at our rear—this is a calamity in the belly and heart.
translations.idiomatic: We are a thousand li from home, fighting far afield, with powerful Yan at our back—that is a knife at the heart.

sentences.zh: 」乃為之班師。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon they withdrew the army for him.
translations.idiomatic: ” For his sake they turned back.

sentences.zh: 守光益以為諸鎮畏其強，乃諷諸鎮共推尊己，於是晉王率天德宋瑤、振武周德威、昭義李嗣昭、義武王處直、成德王镕等，以墨制冊尊守光為尚書令、尚父。

translations.literal: Shouguang thought still more that the circuits feared his strength; he hinted that the circuits jointly exalt him. Thereupon the Prince of Jin led Song Yao of Tiande, Zhou Dewei of Zhenwu, Li Sizhao of Zhaoyi, Wang Chuzhi of Yiwu, Wang Rong of Chengde, and others, with ink edicts enfeoffing Shouguang as Director-in-Chief and Imperial Father.
translations.idiomatic: Shouguang took this as proof that every circuit feared him and began pressing them to elevate him together. The Prince of Jin then had Song Yao of Tiande, Zhou Dewei of Zhenwu, Li Sizhao of Zhaoyi, Wang Chuzhi of Yiwu, Wang Rong of Chengde, and others issue ink edicts naming Shouguang Director-in-Chief and Imperial Father.

sentences.zh: 守光又遣告於梁，請授己河北兵馬都統，以討鎮、定、河東。

translations.literal: Shouguang also sent word to Liang, asking to be appointed commander-in-chief of Hebei military and horse, to attack Zhen, Ding, and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Shouguang also petitioned Liang to make him overall commander of Hebei armies and cavalry, with orders to strike Zhen, Ding, and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 梁遣閣門使王瞳拜守光河北采訪使。

translations.literal: Liang sent Palace Gate Commissioner Wang Tong to invest Shouguang as Hebei outreach commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent palace gate commissioner Wang Tong to invest him Hebei outreach commissioner.

sentences.zh: 有司白守光，尚父受冊，用唐冊太尉禮儀，守光問曰：「此儀註何不郊天改元？

translations.literal: The office reported to Shouguang: receiving investiture as Imperial Father uses Tang ritual for investing the Grand Marshal. Shouguang asked: “Why does this ceremonial note not include sacrificing to Heaven and changing the reign title?
translations.idiomatic: The clerks told Shouguang that an Imperial Father’s investiture followed Tang’s rites for enfeoffing a Grand Marshal. Shouguang demanded: “Why does the manual say nothing about sacrificing to Heaven or changing the era name?

sentences.zh: 」有司曰：「此天子之禮也，尚父雖尊，乃人臣耳。

translations.literal: ” The office said: “That is the Son of Heaven’s ritual; though the Imperial Father is exalted, he is still a subject.
translations.idiomatic: ” They answered: “Those are the Son of Heaven’s rites. However honored the Imperial Father may be, he remains a subject.

sentences.zh: 」守光怒曰：「我為尚父，誰當帝者乎？

translations.literal: ” Shouguang raged: “I am Imperial Father—who would be emperor?
translations.idiomatic: ” Shouguang flared: “I am Imperial Father—who then is emperor?

sentences.zh: 且今天下四分五裂，大者稱帝，小者稱王，我以二千里之燕，獨不能帝一方乎？

translations.literal: Besides, today the realm is split four and five ways; the great call themselves emperors, the small call themselves kings. With my Yan of two thousand li, can I alone not be emperor of one quarter?
translations.idiomatic: The realm is broken four and five ways; the mighty take the title of emperor, the lesser the title of king. With two thousand li of Yan, why should I alone not reign over my quarter?

sentences.zh: 」乃械梁、晉使者下獄，置斧钅質於其庭，令曰：「敢諫者死！

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he fettered Liang and Jin envoys and cast them into prison, set axe and block in his courtyard, and proclaimed: “Whoever dares remonstrate dies!
translations.idiomatic: ” He had Liang and Jin envoys shackled and thrown into prison, set an axe and execution block in the courtyard, and announced: “Whoever advises against this dies!

sentences.zh: 」孫鶴進曰：「滄州之敗，臣蒙王不殺之恩，今日之事，不敢不諫。

translations.literal: ” Sun He advanced and said: “At the defeat at Cangzhou I received the king’s grace of not being killed; for today’s affair I dare not fail to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: ” Sun He stepped forward: “After Cangzhou fell you spared my life. For what you mean to do today I cannot stay silent.

sentences.zh: 」守光怒，推之伏钅質，令軍士割而啖之。

translations.literal: ” Shouguang raged, pushed him down by the block, and ordered the soldiers to cut off pieces and devour him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shouguang had him thrown to the block and ordered the troops to carve off his flesh and eat it.

sentences.zh: 鶴呼曰：「不出百日，大兵當至！

translations.literal: He cried: “Within a hundred days great troops will arrive!
translations.idiomatic: Sun He shouted: “In less than a hundred days a great army will come!

sentences.zh: 」命窒其口而醢之。

translations.literal: ” He was ordered silenced by stuffing his mouth, then minced.
translations.idiomatic: ” They stuffed his mouth and pickled what remained of him.

sentences.zh: 守光遂以梁乾化元年八月自號大燕皇帝，改元曰應天，以王瞳、齊涉為左右相。

translations.literal: Shouguang then in the eighth month of Liang Qianhua year 1 styled himself Great Yan Emperor, changed the era title to Yingtian, and made Wang Tong and Qi She left and right chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Liang Qianhua 1 Shouguang proclaimed himself emperor of Great Yan, declared the era Yingtian, and made Wang Tong and Qi She his left and right chancellors.

sentences.zh: 晉遣太原少尹李承勛賀冊尚父，至燕，而守光已僭號。

translations.literal: Jin sent Taiyuan Vice Governor Li Chengxun to congratulate the investiture as Imperial Father; when he reached Yan, Shouguang had already usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Jin dispatched Li Chengxun, vice governor of Taiyuan, to congratulate the Imperial Father’s investiture; by the time he reached Yan, Shouguang had already seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 有司迫承勛稱臣，承勛不屈，以列國交聘禮入見，守光怒，殺之。

translations.literal: The office pressed Chengxun to call himself subject; he would not bend, entered audience with ritual as between states on embassies. Shouguang raged and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The court forced Chengxun to declare himself a subject. He refused and entered audience by the protocol due a foreign envoy. Shouguang had him killed.

sentences.zh: 明年，晉遣周德威將三萬人，會鎮、定之兵以攻燕，自祈溝關入，其澶、涿、武、順諸州皆迎降。

translations.literal: The next year Jin sent Zhou Dewei with thirty thousand men, joining Zhen and Ding troops to attack Yan. They entered by Qigou Pass; Chan, Zhuo, Wu, Shun, and other prefectures all welcomed and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Jin sent Zhou Dewei with thirty thousand men, joined by the armies of Zhen and Ding, against Yan. They came through Qigou Pass; Chan, Zhuo, Wu, Shun, and the other prefectures opened their gates.

sentences.zh: 守光被圍經年，累戰常敗，乃遣客將王遵化致書於德威曰：「予得罪於晉，迷而不復，今其病矣，公善為我辭焉。

translations.literal: Shouguang was besieged for a year, repeatedly defeated in battle. He sent his client-officer Wang Zunhua with a letter to Dewei: “I have offended Jin, lost my way and will not return; now I am ill. Sir, speak well of me.
translations.idiomatic: Besieged for a year and beaten in fight after fight, Shouguang sent his client-officer Wang Zunhua to Dewei with a letter: “I have wronged Jin and lost my way; now I am sick. Plead my case with your lord.

sentences.zh: 」德威謂遵化曰：「大燕皇帝尚未郊天，何至此邪？

translations.literal: ” Dewei said to Zunhua: “The Great Yan Emperor has not yet sacrificed to Heaven—how has it come to this?
translations.idiomatic: ” Dewei told Zunhua: “The Great Yan Emperor has not yet sacrificed to Heaven—how does he come to such words?

sentences.zh: 予受命以討僭亂，不知其佗也。

translations.literal: I received orders to punish rebellion—nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: My orders are to crush rebellion—nothing more.

sentences.zh: 」守光益窘，乃獻絹千匹、銀千兩、錦百段，遣其將周遵業謂德威曰：「吾王以情告公，富貴成敗，人之常理；

translations.literal: ” Shouguang grew still more desperate, sent a thousand bolts of silk, a thousand taels of silver, a hundred lengths of brocade, and his general Zhou Zunye to tell Dewei: “My lord speaks to you from the heart: fortune and failure are man’s constant lot;
translations.idiomatic: ” Still more cornered, Shouguang sent a thousand bolts of silk, a thousand taels of silver, a hundred lengths of brocade, and his general Zhou Zunye to Dewei with this message: “My lord speaks plainly: rise and fall are the common lot;

sentences.zh: 錄功宥過，霸者之事也。

translations.literal: recording merit and pardoning fault are the business of a hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: to reward service and forgive error is what a hegemon does.

sentences.zh: 守光去歲妄自尊崇，本不能為朱溫下耳，豈意大國暴師經年，幸少寬之。

translations.literal: Last year Shouguang rashly exalted himself; originally he could not bow to Zhu Wen. He never thought the great state would send troops for a year—would you grant a little leniency?
translations.idiomatic: Last year Shouguang overreached; he never meant to serve Zhu Wen. He never imagined your great state would camp here a full year—surely you can show some mercy.

sentences.zh: 」德威不許。

translations.literal: ” Dewei did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: ” Dewei would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 守光登城呼德威曰：「公三晉賢士，獨不急人之危乎？

translations.literal: Shouguang climbed the wall and called to Dewei: “You are a worthy man of the Three Jins—will you alone not hurry to save a man in peril?
translations.idiomatic: Shouguang mounted the wall and cried to Dewei: “You are a worthy of the Three Jins—will you not aid a man at the edge of ruin?

sentences.zh: 」遣人以所乘馬易德威馬而去，因告曰：「俟晉王至則降。

translations.literal: ” He sent someone to exchange the horse he rode for Dewei’s horse and leave, and furthermore said: “When the Prince of Jin arrives I shall surrender.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sent a man to swap his own mount for Dewei’s and ride off, adding: “When the Prince of Jin comes, I will submit.

sentences.zh: 」晉王乃自臨軍，守光登城見晉王，晉王問將如何？

translations.literal: ” The Prince of Jin then came in person to the army. Shouguang climbed the wall and saw the Prince; the Prince asked how it would be.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Prince of Jin came to the camp in person. Shouguang looked down from the wall; the Prince asked what he intended.

sentences.zh: 守光曰：「今日俎上肉耳，惟王所為也！

translations.literal: Shouguang said: “Today I am meat on the chopping block—do as you will!
translations.idiomatic: Shouguang said: “I am meat on the block—do with me as you please!

sentences.zh: 」守光有嬖者李小喜，勸其毋降，守光因請俟佗日。

translations.literal: ” Shouguang had a favorite Li Xiaoxi who urged him not to surrender; Shouguang therefore asked to wait another day.
translations.idiomatic: ” His favorite Li Xiaoxi urged him to hold out; Shouguang asked for one more day.

sentences.zh: 是夕，小喜叛降於晉軍。

translations.literal: That night Xiaoxi defected to the Jin army.
translations.idiomatic: That night Xiaoxi slipped over to Jin.

sentences.zh: 明旦，晉軍攻破其城，執仁恭及其家族三百口。

translations.literal: At dawn the Jin army broke the city and seized Rengong and his clan, three hundred mouths.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Jin stormed the city and took Rengong and three hundred members of his house.

sentences.zh: 守光與其妻李氏、祝氏，子繼珣、繼方、繼祚等，南走滄州，迷失道，至燕樂界中，數日不得食，遣其妻祝氏乞食於田家，田家怪而詰之，祝氏以實告，乃被擒送幽州。

translations.literal: Shouguang with his wife Lady Li, Lady Zhu, sons Jixun, Jifang, Jizuo, fled south toward Cangzhou, lost the road, reached the border of Yan and Le, several days without food. He sent his wife Lady Zhu to beg food from a farm household; the family found it strange and questioned her; she told the truth—they were seized and sent to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shouguang fled south toward Cangzhou with Lady Li, Lady Zhu, and his sons Jixun, Jifang, and Jizuo. They lost the road and wandered the borderlands of Yan and Le, days without food. He sent Lady Zhu to beg at a farmhouse; the farmers questioned her, she confessed, and they were seized and sent to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉王方大饗軍，客將引守光見，晉王戲之曰：「主人何避客之遽也？

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin was feasting the army. The client-officer led Shouguang in to audience. The Prince jested: “How quickly the host avoids his guest!
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin was feasting the troops when Shouguang was brought in. He mocked him: “Why does the host flee his guest so fast?

sentences.zh: 」守光叩頭請死，命械守光並其父仁恭以從軍。

translations.literal: ” Shouguang kowtowed begging death. He ordered Shouguang fettered together with his father Rengong to follow the army.
translations.idiomatic: ” Shouguang kowtowed and begged for death. The Prince had him shackled to his father Rengong and marched them with the army.

sentences.zh: 軍還過趙，趙王王镕會晉王，置酒，酒酣請曰：「願見仁恭父子。

translations.literal: The army returned passing through Zhao. Zhao king Wang Rong met the Prince of Jin and set out wine. When the wine was heated he requested: “I would see father and son Rengong.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home through Zhao, Wang Rong entertained the Prince of Jin. When the cups were warm he asked: “Let me see Rengong and his son.

sentences.zh: 」晉王命破械出之，引置下坐。

translations.literal: ” The Prince ordered their fetters broken and them brought out, seated below him.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Prince had their bonds removed and them brought out to sit below the dais.

sentences.zh: 飲食自若，皆無慚色。

translations.literal: They ate and drank as usual, all without shame.
translations.idiomatic: They ate and drank as if nothing had happened, without a trace of shame.

sentences.zh: 晉王至太原，仁恭父子曳以組練，獻於太廟。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin reached Taiyuan; father and son Rengong were dragged in cord fetters and presented at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: At Taiyuan the Prince had father and son Rengong dragged forward in ropes and presented at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 守光將死，泣曰：「臣死無恨，然教臣不降者，李小喜也，罪人不死，臣將訴於地下。

translations.literal: Shouguang about to die wept: “Your subject dies without regret; yet he who taught your subject not to surrender was Li Xiaoxi. If the guilty man does not die, your subject will plead below.
translations.idiomatic: Facing execution, Shouguang wept: “I die without complaint—but the man who told me not to surrender was Li Xiaoxi. If he lives, I will accuse him in the underworld.

sentences.zh: 」晉王使召小喜，小喜瞋目曰：「囚父弒兄，蒸其骨肉，亦小喜教爾邪？

translations.literal: ” The Prince of Jin sent to summon Xiaoxi. Xiaoxi glared and said: “You imprisoned your father, murdered your brother, steamed your kin to eat—is that too Xiaoxi’s teaching?
translations.idiomatic: ” The Prince summoned Xiaoxi. Xiaoxi glared: “You jailed your father, killed your brother, boiled your own flesh for food—did I teach you that?

sentences.zh: 」晉王怒，命先斬小喜。

translations.literal: ” The Prince raged and ordered Xiaoxi executed first.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Prince ordered Xiaoxi beheaded first.

sentences.zh: 守光知不免，呼曰：「王將復唐室以成霸業，何不赦臣使自效？

translations.literal: Shouguang knew he could not escape, cried: “My lord will restore the Tang to accomplish hegemony—why not pardon your subject to serve you?
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not live, Shouguang cried: “You mean to restore Tang and build an empire—why not spare me and use me?

sentences.zh: 」其二婦從旁罵曰：「事已至此，生復何為？

translations.literal: ” His two consorts cursed from beside him: “Things have come to this—what is life for?
translations.idiomatic: ” His two wives cursed from the side: “It has come to this—what is there to live for?

sentences.zh: 願先死！

translations.literal: We wish to die first!
translations.idiomatic: Let us die first!

sentences.zh: 」乃俱死。

translations.literal: ” And all died together.
translations.idiomatic: ” All three were executed together.

sentences.zh: 晉王命李存霸執仁恭至雁門，刺其心血以祭先王墓，然後斬之。

translations.literal: The Prince ordered Li Cunba to escort Rengong to Yanmen, pierce his heart’s blood to sacrifice at the former prince’s tomb, then behead him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince sent Li Cunba to take Rengong to Yanmen, draw blood from his heart to offer at the tomb of the late Prince, and then behead him.
